guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: the few existing photos of Robert Johnson show him with a Gibson L-1 acoustic, a commonly cited association in blues history.
guitar.notes: Documented via the famous photographs, though gear history overall for Johnson is sparse given era.

tone.target: 1936 solo acoustic blues, dry room mic
tone.profile: 1936 solo acoustic blues, dry room mic
tone.summary: A highly controlled, clean signal chain utilizing compression and a low-gain amp (US Deluxe) paired with a small, focused cabinet (US 2x12) to emulate the close-mic'd, dry resonance of an acoustic guitar in a pre-war blues setting.

rig.name: Robert Johnson - Cross Road Blues - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain a tight signal for fingerpicking.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean tones.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the attack transients and sustain, mimicking the percussive nature of fingerpicking.
Keep the signal clean and transparent to maintain acoustic character.
Provide a clean, articulate tone suitable for vintage blues without excessive coloration.
blocks.gap: The US Deluxe is the closest available model to a clean, non-tube amp sound needed for this dry acoustic simulation.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the close-mic'd, focused resonance of a single acoustic source.
blocks.gap: The US 2x12 is chosen for its smaller footprint and ability to focus on midrange detail, mimicking a close mic setup better than larger cabs.

blocks.purpose: Sculpt the frequency response to emphasize the brittle steel-string midrange and remove muddy low end.
blocks.gap: None. Essential for tone shaping in acoustic simulations.

blocks.purpose: No wah needed; the focus must remain on pure acoustic tone.
blocks.gap: N/A. Avoids any colored filtering that distracts from the source material.

blocks.purpose: No modulation effects (Chorus/Tremolo) are appropriate for the dry, vintage blues sound.
blocks.gap: N/A. Keeps the tone raw and natural.

blocks.purpose: Avoid delay to maintain the dry, immediate feel of a pre-war recording.
blocks.gap: N/A. Delay adds space and time, which is contrary to the 'dry room' mandate.

blocks.purpose: Provide the absolute minimum amount of natural room ambience without sounding like a modern reverb tail.
blocks.gap: The 'minimal room ambience' requirement is met by setting the Room Reverb mix extremely low, simulating only the immediate acoustic space.

improvements.summary: Replace the generic cabinet IR with one that specifically models close-mic'd acoustic guitar resonance to better capture the brittle, dry midrange of vintage recordings.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Vintage Acoustic Body IR (e.g., specific Martin/Gibson model)
proposals.reason: The current US 2x12 is too generic; a dedicated acoustic IR will better capture the required brittle, dry midrange and close-mic character.
proposals.expectedGain: Improved realism of source instrument tone
